newsitem.title: USA: Kodak sees difficulty growing FY97 oper EPS.
newsitem.headline: Kodak sees difficulty growing FY97 oper EPS.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said Wednesday it sees difficulties in growing its fiscal year 1997 operating earnings per share beyond fiscal year 1996 levels.

The company said all its units will accelerate their ongoing cost reduction programs. It also said it remains committed to growing its digital portfolio, although losses from digital products increased during the second quarter.

The company said earnings for the second quarter were hurt by the strength of the U.S. dollar, higher losses for digital products, continued higher marketing expenses to support the new Advantix system and price pressures.
Kodak reported earnings per share of $1.12 compared with $1.30 for the same period a year ago. The First Call estimate for the quarter was $1.39 per share.
In pre-morning trading, the company's stock was trading at 73, off 3-14/16.
The company said the reason for its difficulty in growing operating earnings is heavy investment in marketing of its Advantix products and in its digital products and services.
Kodak also said it is the result of continuing problems executing some business plans and the impact of adverse foreign exchange and an intensifying competitive environment.
Over the long term, the company said it remains committed to its earnings objective of an average of at least a 10 percent earnings per share increase per year.
